chapter: Childhood in Tyler, Beaumont and Houston
title: Friendship with the Dewalt family and their records
summary: Gus and Olin become like brothers, he goes on family vacations, hears their many records, and sees Olin's violin lessons fail.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: That was the first time I saw my name up. And the Dewalds, well, they knew I liked drums, too.
And his son and I, we were just very close friends.
They'd take a vacation, they would take me.
Because he was an only, too.
He was the only one. And I was one of his best friends.
That was fortunate. You were a lucky guy, weren't you?
Yeah. Yeah, one thing followed another.
So you were gaining experience and learning something, sitting in the pit there.
And, of course, you were hearing music all the time.
I was listening to good music all the time.
Yeah. Well, now, this was where you'd hear some records as well.
Oh, they had a lot of records.
Because Olin, he was taking violin
My mother wanted me to take violin. But I couldn't stand it. I just couldn't stand that squeaking, to me.
Yeah, it's far from being a rhythm instrument.
Oh, yes. And he had one of the best teachers. He had a German teacher, teaching him violin lessons. But he never learned to play the violin.
He didn't go for it, either.
Not really. And I used to see his teacher, and I'd be over there. And his teacher would be hollering at him all the time about, "Do this and do this right." And so he just gave up on him.
Yeah. So he never went on to do anything else;
Well, he must have kind of admired the way you were getting on as a drummer.
Oh, yes, and we were just like two brothers, really.
